In 1882, a man was found dead under an oak tree in Arizona. Revolver in his hand. Boots gone. Part of his scalp cut away. The jury called it suicide.

His name was Johnny Ringo, and almost nobody believes the jury. Wyatt Earp? Doc Holliday? A gambler with a grudge? Who do you think did it? 👇

The full documentary is on YouTube: link in bio.

America just got its 64th national park, and most people have never heard of it.

27 million years ago an eruption 1,000 times bigger than Mount St. Helens buried this place in ash. Ice and time carved it into thousands of stone spires, balanced boulders, and a mountain shaped like a face. A wild jaguar has walked these canyons.

This is Chiricahua. Would you go? 🏜️

1886. The Army loaded nearly every Chiricahua Apache onto prison trains, even the scouts who had served it.

Somewhere in Missouri, one man jumped. Alone, in country he had never seen, Massai walked hundreds of miles back to the mountains, traveling only at night. Today the highest viewpoint in America's newest national park carries his name.

The full documentary is on YouTube: link in bio.
